We have many templates. Need the one that corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation. The retro template should break a C-Cl bond and form an acyl chloride? Actually forward: aromatic + acyl chloride -> aromatic-CO-R + HCl. Retrosynthesis: aromatic-CO-R -> aromatic + acyl chloride (RCOCl). So precursors: aromatic ring (same as product but without acyl group) and acyl chloride.

Thus we need to apply appropriate template to target molecule (the given SMILES). The target is a complex molecule with many groups; but the specific transformation likely is at a particular aromatic ring where an acyl group attached via C=O-N? Wait the target SMILES: COc1ccc(CNc2c(C(=O)Nc3cccc(OC)c3)nnn2Cc2ccc(CN3CC(F)C3)cc2)cc1

It contains a C(=O)N attached to heterocycle. Not a simple acyl group on aromatic. Friedel-Crafts acylation would give aromatic-CO-R (aryl ketone). Here we have amide attached to heterocycle. Might not be Friedel-Crafts. But the task says "apply the template as the result of the task make_6_lvl2-template_search-2". That template is the one we need to apply. The template_search-2 task failed earlier. But we now have many templates; which one is the correct one? The description: "The Friedel-Crafts acylation is a type of electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction that introduces an acyl group onto an aromatic ring. The reaction typically involves the use of an acyl chloride (RCOCl) in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst... An 'halide' functional group is gone during the transformation."

Thus the template should involve a halide (Cl) leaving from aromatic carbon, and an acyl group being attached. Look at templates that have Cl on aromatic side in reactants. For retro, product is aromatic with carbonyl attached, reactants are aromatic with Cl and acyl chloride.

Search among results: entry 1914393 retro_smarts_template: '[#7:7]-[C:6]-[c:5]1:[c:4]:[c:3]:[c:2](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:12]2:[#7;a:11]:[#7;a:10]:[c:14]:[c:13]:2):[c:9]:[c:8]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]1:[c:3]:[c:4]:[c:5](-[C:6]-[#7:7]):[c:8]:[c:9]:1.[#7;a:10]1:[#7;a:11]:[nH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:[c:14]:1'

This seems to break a C-Cl bond on aromatic and produce a side chain with Cl-CH2 attached? Not typical.

Entry 96922: retro: '[c:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:7]1:[#7;a:3]:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].[#7;a:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:[nH;D2;+0:7]:1' This is halogen on side chain, not aromatic carbonyl.

Entry 82460 similar with Br.

Entry 1838006: retro: '[O;D1;H0:4]=[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[c:5])-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]>>C-C-C(=O)-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].Cl-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;D1;H0:4])-[c:5]' This seems to break a C-Cl bond on aromatic carbon attached to carbonyl (acyl chloride). The product side is aromatic amide? Actually forward: aromatic amide + acyl chloride -> aromatic amide with acyl group? Not exactly.

But this template seems plausible: It takes aromatic amide (C(=O)N attached to aromatic) and splits into aromatic amine and acyl chloride. That matches Friedel-Crafts acylation? Not exactly because Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl to aromatic directly, not via amide. However the template includes an amide nitrogen attached to aromatic, which is not typical.

Maybe the correct template is 1838006. Let's apply it to target molecule to see if it matches.

We need template_id. We have template_hash but not ID. We can retrieve template by ID? The tool get_template requires template_id. We don't have ID. But maybe we can use apply_template with template_id as the hash? Not sure. Usually template_id is some identifier. Could be the template_hash. Let's try apply_template with template_id = the hash.

Target SMILES: COc1ccc(CNc2c(C(=O)Nc3cccc(OC)c3)nnn2Cc2ccc(CN3CC(F)C3)cc2)cc1

Use apply_template.
